title: HubSpot vs SuiteCRM
comparison_markdown:
# HubSpot vs SuiteCRM (2026)

## Overview
HubSpot and SuiteCRM are two popular customer relationship management (CRM) tools that help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses, entrepreneurs, and marketing teams who want to switch from a proprietary CRM to a self-hosted, open-source solution. The core use case for both tools is to streamline sales and marketing processes, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: HubSpot offers a free plan and several paid plans, while SuiteCRM is free and open-source, with optional paid support.
* Data ownership: With SuiteCRM, users have full ownership and control over their data, while HubSpot stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: HubSpot is generally easier to set up and use, while SuiteCRM requires more technical expertise to self-host and customize.
* Scalability: HubSpot is designed for large enterprises and can handle a high volume of users and data, while SuiteCRM is better suited for small to medium-sized businesses.
* Integration: HubSpot has native integration with Google Calendar, while SuiteCRM requires a third-party plugin to achieve similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | HubSpot | SuiteCRM |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $15-$800+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $45-$90/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $180-$360/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**HubSpot:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Robust marketing and sales automation features
* Good customer support
* Integrates well with other HubSpot tools
* Limited customization options
**SuiteCRM:**
* Free and open-source
* Highly customizable
* Self-hosting option for data control
* Community-driven development
* Steeper learning curve

## When to Choose Each
HubSpot is a good choice for large enterprises or businesses that need robust marketing and sales automation features, and are willing to pay for them. It's also a good option for teams that want an easy-to-use, cloud-based CRM with good customer support. SuiteCRM, on the other hand, is suitable for small to medium-sized businesses, entrepreneurs, or teams that want a high degree of customization and control over their data, and are willing to invest time in setting it up and learning its features.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from HubSpot in CSV format.
2. Install and set up SuiteCRM on your server.
3. Use the SuiteCRM import tool to import your data from the CSV file.
4. Configure your SuiteCRM instance to match your business needs.
5. Test and verify that your data has been imported correctly.

## Our Take
SuiteCRM is a production-ready CRM solution for most users, but it may require more technical expertise to set up and customize than HubSpot. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that SuiteCRM's reporting features are not as robust as HubSpot's, and may require additional configuration to get the desired insights. Overall, we recommend switching to SuiteCRM if you're a small to medium-sized business or entrepreneur who wants a high degree of control over your data and customization options, and are willing to invest time in setting it up.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users who don't need advanced marketing automation features
* Entrepreneurs who want a free, self-hosted CRM solution
* Teams with limited budgets who want to reduce their CRM costs
* Businesses that require a high degree of customization and control over their data
* Organizations with existing IT infrastructure who want to self-host their CRM

## FAQ
### Is SuiteCRM free?
Yes, SuiteCRM is free and open-source, with optional paid support.
### Can I self-host HubSpot?
No, HubSpot is a cloud-based CRM and cannot be self-hosted.
### Does SuiteCRM have a mobile app?
Yes, SuiteCRM has a mobile app for Android and iOS devices.
### Can I import my data from HubSpot to SuiteCRM?
Yes, you can export your data from HubSpot in CSV format and import it into SuiteCRM using the import tool.
### Is SuiteCRM suitable for large enterprises?
Not yet, SuiteCRM is better suited for small to medium-sized businesses, but it can be customized to meet the needs of larger organizations.
meta_description: SuiteCRM, a free, self-hosted CRM, offers more control and customization than HubSpot. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

# Mailchimp vs Listmonk (2026)

## Overview
Mailchimp and Listmonk are both email marketing tools that help businesses manage their email campaigns and subscriber lists. This comparison is beneficial for marketers, small business owners, and entrepreneurs who want to switch from a proprietary, paid solution to a self-hosted, free alternative. The core use case for both tools is email marketing automation, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Mailchimp offers a free plan with limited features, while Listmonk is completely free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Listmonk allows users to retain full ownership of their data, while Mailchimp's terms of service grant the company permission to use and distribute user data.
* Setup complexity: Mailchimp has a more user-friendly interface and easier setup process, while Listmonk requires more technical expertise to set up and configure.
* Scalability: Listmonk is designed to be highly scalable and can handle large volumes of email traffic, while Mailchimp's scalability is limited by its pricing plans.
* Integration with e-commerce platforms: Mailchimp has native integrations with popular e-commerce platforms like Shopify and WooCommerce, while Listmonk requires third-party plugins or custom integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Mailchimp | Listmonk |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $13-$350+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $13/month (Essentials plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $350+/month (Pro plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons

* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of templates and design tools
* Robust automation features
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data and customization options
**Listmonk:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Highly customizable and scalable
* Full control over data and ownership
* Open-source community support
* Steeper learning curve and more technical expertise required

Listmonk, on the other hand, is ideal for larger teams or organizations that require a high degree of customization, scalability, and control over their data. ## Migration Path

2. Set up a new Listmonk instance on your server or hosting platform.

## Our Take

However, for teams that value data ownership, scalability, and customization, Listmonk is definitely worth considering, and we recommend switching from Mailchimp to Listmonk for those who prioritize these features.

## Who Should Switch
* Small business owners with fewer than 10 employees who don't need advanced automation features

Yes, you can export your email list from Mailchimp in CSV format and import it into Listmonk using the built-in import tool.

title: WordPress.com vs Ghost
comparison_markdown:
# WordPress.com vs Ghost

## Overview

Hosted blogging and website platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Ghost is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: WordPress.com costs Free / $4-$45+/month; Ghost is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: WordPress.com is Proprietary; Ghost is MIT
- **Data ownership**: Ghost can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Ghost eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Ghost has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | WordPress.com | Ghost |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $4-$45+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### WordPress.com

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Ghost

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [TryGhost/Ghost](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost) * ~47k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose WordPress.com if:** WordPress.com is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Ghost if:** Ghost is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from WordPress.com in its standard export format, review Ghost import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Ghost is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid WordPress.com tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Ghost instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for WordPress.com, switching to self-hosted Ghost will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on WordPress.com until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated WordPress.com paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Ghost free to use?
Yes. Ghost is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from WordPress.com to Ghost?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your WordPress.com data, follow the Ghost import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Ghost get regular updates?
Yes. Ghost has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Ghost without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Ghost development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced August 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [WordPress.com](https://wordpress.com) and [Ghost](https://ghost.org) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Ghost is a free, self-hosted alternative to WordPress.com. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.
